question: Does reusing the unchanged current-main reward-card pool remove offer-path drift while preserving two functionally distinct package routes for each aspect?

shippingChangesAtThisStage: Keep the current-main card catalogue and reward pools unchanged.
Flicker applies Scoreline for Faultline to consume; Mirrorlight applies Afterimage for Warden's Edge to consume.
Keep the admitted Ash Bloodfire and Mistbound mediators unchanged.

researchCohorts.cemTrain: six Duskblade-v5 islands, generations 0-5, eight CRN seeds per generation, 173000-173047
researchCohorts.finalValidation: all six frozen final policies, paired candidate/live, 175000-175063

priorMechanicEvidence.scope: V15 admits the two Ash mediator identities only as prior evidence. Both Dusk producer-consumer identities changed, so v16 reruns every local and whole-run gate with fresh cohorts.

competingOptions.statement: An unchanged offer pool removes path drift while all four mediator packages and Dusk endpoints pass.
Functional separation, endpoint viability, reliability, retention or the Vow-5 ceiling fails.

estimands.optimisation: Six independent existing-tool CEM islands maximise eight-seed generation win rate; no holdout or final-validation result feeds fitting.
estimands.routeViability: For each assigned route, at least two final policies activate that mediator and exceed held-out RandomBuild arm 2 by at least 0.35 on fresh final-validation seeds.
estimands.retention: At least two distinct final policies remain within 0.10 of the overall top, and route-best rates remain within 0.10.
estimands.reliability: No CEM holdout simulator fault and no candidate-added stall or simulator error on paired final validation.
estimands.vow5: Every final-policy validation win rate is at most 0.90.

successRule.routeViability: At least two independently fitted final policies per assigned route meet activation and the 0.35 C2 margin.
successRule.retention: Both assigned routes retain high-performing distinct endpoints without one-route collapse.
successRule.reliability: No CEM holdout stall/error, no candidate-added final-validation stall, and zero simulator errors.
successRule.vow5: All final-policy win rates are at most 0.90.

cheapestDiscriminatingExperiment: Run 32-pair scripted separation and policy panels first. If both continue, run their independent 32-pair validation; only an inconclusive policy panel may extend once to 128. Then run controls and the existing six-island mini-CEM with fresh cohorts.
inconclusiveRule: Only a non-decisive policy-panel result may extend once from 32 to 128 pairs. The six-island CEM and 64-seed final rectangle are final for v16; no island replacement, extra generation, reselection or content change is allowed.
stopRule: Reject if local separation or activation fails, broad movement or a fault fails controls, fewer than two policies per route meet held-out activation and C2, endpoints collapse, an added stall/error appears, or Vow-5 exceeds 0.90. Detector mutations remain forbidden until the repertoire passes.
